answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable bond before it may submit bids or vote, then slash that bond when a randomly audited claim fails or colluding agents are proven to double-spend trust. The bond makes identities costly to multiply: an attacker must tie up real capital for every sybil and risks losing it, while reputation accrues only through verified work. A reef-monitoring task might pay in timber credits, with each agent’s pulse of activity checked against signed sensor records.
